the-lives-of-the-twelve-caesars-volume-1: After Nero's fall nearly tore Rome apart, the plainspoken general Vespasian restored order and founded a new dynasty. Suetonius shows a practical, unpretentious ruler — the man who began building the Colosseum and famously joked on his deathbed that he was becoming a god. A refreshing portrait of competence after so many monsters.

The last of the Flavian emperors, Domitian began his reign with promise and ended it as a feared tyrant. Suetonius describes a ruler who demanded to be addressed as a god, surrounded himself with spies, and was finally murdered by his own household in 96 AD. A chilling ancient study of how absolute power warps a man.
the-rover-boys-on-the-great-lakes-or-the: Edward Stratemeyer's famous Rover Boys — Tom, Sam, and Dick — take their adventures to the Great Lakes in this installment of the long-running series. A secret island cave, lurking villains, and narrow escapes keep the brothers busy from shore to shore. Pure turn-of-the-century boy's adventure, delivered at Stratemeyer's reliable gallop.
the-iron-woman: Margaret Deland's novel centers on a formidable matriarch — the iron woman — whose strong will shapes everyone around her, especially her son. As the younger generation pushes against her control, the story asks what strength costs and what it saves. Deland's sympathetic, searching fiction made her one of America's most respected novelists.
personal-experience-of-a-physician: Dr. John Ellis looks back on a lifetime of medical practice in this candid nineteenth-century memoir. He writes of the diseases he fought, the patients he knew, and how medicine changed across his career — from bleeding and blistering to modern science. A rare, human-scale record of what doctoring was really like in a bygone age.
myths-and-legends-of-our-own-land-volume: New England's stern Puritan past yields Salem witches, haunted parsonages, and spectral ships in this volume. Skinner draws on the region's deep stock of eerie colonial tales, told with a relish for the supernatural. The perfect book for a dark evening — America's oldest ghost stories, gathered with care.
from-the-caves-and-jungles-of-hindostan: Helena Blavatsky — the controversial founder of Theosophy — recounts her travels through India in these vivid letters. Temples, jungles, fakirs, and alleged marvels fill pages that blend travel writing with mystical speculation. Whether believed or doubted, the book offers a fascinating view of India through extraordinary eyes.
observations-of-a-retired-veteran: Henry Tinsley looks back on a soldier's life in these plain-spoken recollections. Battles, camp life, and the long aftermath of war are remembered without romance but with deep feeling. Such veterans' memoirs preserve the human reality behind the history books' grand strategies.
memoirs-of-the-life-of-the-rt-hon-richar: Poet Thomas Moore writes the life of his friend Richard Brinsley Sheridan — playwright of The School for Scandal, orator, and wit. This first volume covers his dazzling rise in theater and Parliament. Moore's affectionate, elegant biography remains a key source on one of Georgian England's most brilliant figures.
adventures-in-the-land-of-canaan: R. L. Berry's Sunday-school adventure brings Bible lands to life for young readers — the hills, vales, and towns where the old stories were lived. Godly, bright, and full of teaching, it weds faith to map-work. A glad trek through the Holy Land for young pilgrims.
paula-the-waldensian: Eva Lecomte tells of Paula, a child of the Waldensians — the ancient Alpine folk who kept their faith through centuries of persecution. Her story lights up a little-known corner of church history. Brave, touching, and true to its sources.
tramping-through-mexico-guatemala-and-ho: Harry Franck, the prince of vagabond travelers, tramps through Mexico and Central America with a knapsack, small cash, and an open eye. His random notes catch lands few tourists ever saw — markets, ruins, and roadside folk. Lively, observant travel writing at its best.
the-coral-island-a-tale-of-the-pacific-o: R. M. Ballantyne's immortal boys' book strands Ralph, Jack, and Peterkin on a coral island — pirates, cannibals, and wild adventure follow. The tale that inspired Treasure Island and Lord of the Flies. The classic castaway story for boys. Three boys, one island, and endless perils made this the pattern for all castaway tales.
sweet-cicely-or-josiah-allen-as-a-politi: Marietta Holley, the beloved Samantha Allen, sends her shrewd farm wife's husband Josiah into politics in this funny, pointed novel. Sweet Cicely's story carries Holley's witty war on bosses, booze, and the bosses' booze. Temperance fiction with a twinkle, loved by millions.
the-shopkeeper-turned-gentleman: Molière's Bourgeois Gentilhomme — the shopkeeper who would be a gentleman — apes his betters to hilarious effect. The prose-speaking joke is immortal. French comedy's greatest triumph. Dancing masters, tailors, and philosophers fleece him to perfection. Music lessons, fine clothes, and would-be wit make him the age's immortal fool.
memoir-and-letters-of-francis-w-newman: Isabel Sieveking gathers the memoir and letters of Francis Newman — scholar, reformer, and brother of the Cardinal. His restless conscience led him through many causes. A revealing portrait of Victorian doubt and idealism. His brave heterodoxy cost him friends but won him a place in history.
the-wishing-ring-man: Margaret Widdemer, the Pulitzer-winning poet of The Old Road to Paradise, spins the tale of the Wishing-Ring Man — a whimsical romance of wishes granted, hearts tested, and love at last found. Her light, lyrical touch charms every page. A delightful bit of early twentieth-century whimsy for romantic readers.
the-koran-al-qur-an: George Sale's translation of the Koran — the first clear English rendering, published in 1734 — opened Islam's holy book to Western readers. His work shaped centuries of European understanding, for better and worse. A landmark of translation and of East-West encounter.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abbey-of-dund: This 1913 Catholic Encyclopedia article on the Abbey of Dundrennan — the Cistercian house where Mary Queen of Scots spent her last Scottish night — tells its romantic story. Oswald Hunter-Blair writes its history. A poignant reference on a Galloway ruin. Mary's ride to the Solway began at its gate.
